narrator.name: Hippius (SN75)
narrator.role: Subnet team, The Nerve Lab; community presenters Mog and Dubs speak for it on podcasts
narrator.one_line: Decentralised cloud storage subnet launched in March 2025 by The Nerve Lab, running its own Substrate chain and Arion erasure-coded storage with an S3-compatible front end; its 2025 writing calls it the storage Bittensor lacked, its 2026 docs sell storage without AWS and barely name Bittensor at all.

statements.quote: A comprehensive Bittensor subnet providing distributed storage, compute, and blockchain management capabilities.
statements.context: Repository description of thenervelab/thebrain, the Hippius chain codebase, read 15 September 2026; the repository dates from the 2025 launch.

statements.quote: Hippius is a Bittensor subnet that enables decentralized file storage and computation across the network. It leverages Bittensor's incentive mechanism while using a network of miners and validators to ensure secure and reliable data management.
statements.context: Opening of the thenervelab/thebrain README, describing how the subnet relates to Bittensor.

statements.quote: a groundbreaking decentralized cloud storage platform built on Bittensor. Subnet, launched on March 11, 2025
statements.context: The team's introductory essay on its Discourse forum, posted by the Hippius account; the essay's opening description, punctuation as in the original.

metaphors.label: platform
metaphors.wording: a groundbreaking decentralized cloud storage platform built on Bittensor
metaphors.lineage_notes: Cloud-vendor language; the team compares itself to AWS and Google Cloud rather than to other subnets.

metaphors.label: competition
metaphors.wording: fosters healthy competition, holding miners accountable
metaphors.lineage_notes: Foundation framing; used once, softened by healthy.

metaphors.label: self-healing
metaphors.lineage_notes: Arion is the team's name for its erasure-coded storage layer.

metaphors.label: ledger
metaphors.wording: Bittensor tracks transaction and service delivery, so you know exactly what you're getting
metaphors.lineage_notes: Bittensor as an audit trail rather than as a market or brain; a third party (Uphold's Scott Guttenberger) reports the team's internal codename was The Brain and the positioning was a memory layer for Bittensor, but no primary carries that wording.

foundation.mission.summary: Provide decentralised file storage and computation across the Bittensor network, using its incentive mechanism with miners and validators.

foundation.vision.summary: Build the future of cloud computing by pushing the boundaries of decentralised storage.

foundation.values.summary: Transparency and user control of data.

problem.market.summary: Bittensor lacked robust decentralised storage and traceability; centralised storage lacks transparency and exposes data to breaches.

opportunity.summary: The gap in the network's own stack: no storage layer before March 2025.

audience.summary: Developers who want S3 storage from any client with no wallet or KYC, and users who pay in fiat or TAO.

positioning.category.summary: A decentralised cloud storage platform and a Bittensor subnet for storage and compute.

positioning.differentiator.summary: Proof of stored data and uptime rather than raw capacity, self-healing erasure-coded storage, and an on-chain record of what was delivered.

positioning.reason.summary: Bittensor's incentive mechanism and its ledger of transactions and service delivery.

positioning.against.summary: Centralised storage systems and named hyperscalers: AWS, Google Cloud, any single company.

value.functional.summary: Secure, transparent, scalable hosting through IPFS and S3-compatible storage, files, websites and VMs, paid in fiat or TAO.

messaging.h1.summary: The solution to storage on Bittensor; transparent and decentralised cloud storage without relying on any single company.

voice.summary: Cloud-vendor marketing prose (groundbreaking, redefine, pushing the boundaries) and practical onboarding lines (no KYC, no wallet required).

language.term.summary: Arion, self-healing storage, hAlpha, credits; the team runs its own chain and token alongside the subnet.

subnet.self.summary: A decentralised cloud storage platform on its own Substrate chain, with miners proven by stored data and uptime, IPFS and S3-compatible front ends, and erasure-coded Arion storage; sold as cloud without AWS.

subnet.network.summary: Bittensor is the base the platform is built on and the incentive mechanism it leverages; it is also the network that lacked storage, and on the 2026 homepage a payment rail and audit trail. The 2026 docs barely name it.

words_avoided: alpha token as a selling point
AI in product copy beyond a model registry

coinages.meaning: Hippius's erasure-coded storage layer: files split into 30 shards, any 10 reconstruct.

coinages.term: the solution to storage on Bittensor
coinages.meaning: The docs tagline claiming the storage niche within the network.

genealogy.summary: In 2025 the team wrote as a Bittensor subnet: a comprehensive subnet for storage and compute that leverages Bittensor's incentive mechanism, arriving because Bittensor lacked robust decentralised storage, with miners held to proof of stored data and uptime [sn75-001] [sn75-002] [sn75-004] [sn75-005]. The formula built on Bittensor and powered by our blockchain recurs [sn75-009].

By 2026 the docs say Hippius is the solution to storage on Bittensor and then describe storage without AWS, Google Cloud or any single company, with sign-up by Google or GitHub and no wallet; the homepage names Bittensor as a way to pay and as the ledger that tracks service delivery [sn75-010] [sn75-011] [sn75-012] [sn75-013].
genealogy.shift: From subnet-first to cloud-vendor-first; Bittensor becomes a payment and audit rail behind an S3 product.

relations.note: Leverages Bittensor's incentive mechanism is foundation-docs phrasing.
Both subnets front a conventional product (S3 storage, a coding agent) and push the network to the background in customer copy.
